basics.name: Robert DeRose
basics.label: Systems & Platform Engineering | Embedded Linux & IoT
basics.summary:
I build the software that bridges hardware and the cloud: embedded Linux, IoT device management, mesh messaging, and the CI/CD that ships it. Seventeen years across Python, Java, Elixir, Go, Rust, TypeScript, and Nix: the right tool for each job.

For 3 years I've been the sole engineer behind SFERO, Checkpoint's best-selling new product, and the CI/CD the whole company ships on. Since 2025 I've worked agent-first with models from Anthropic and OpenAI, using spec-driven development and Beads. Working this way, I made a ~64K-line custom DDS messaging prototype unnecessary by packaging Zenoh with an MQTT bridge in ~2 weeks, and rewrote our RFID platform in my spare time.

work.name: Checkpoint Systems
work.summary: Sole engineer leading SFERO, Checkpoint's best-selling new product, for 3+ years; build the shared embedded Linux, messaging, and release infrastructure.
highlights: Replaced a colleague's multicast-based messaging proof of concept, ~64K lines of custom Data Distribution Service (DDS) code built over 5 months, with a packaged Zenoh/MQTT platform in ~2 weeks: added mutual TLS (mTLS) across the device fleet, adapted their per-application leader election, and built a React operator console

Rewrote our RFID loss-prevention platform from scratch in Elixir/OTP in my spare time over ~3.5 months, using OTP's distribution and fault tolerance for restart-safe alarm processing that never replays an alarm, and alarm strategies operators can change without new code, in the UI or through APIs for external integrators

Upgraded every UI from React 17 and PatternFly 4 to React 19 and PatternFly 6 on Vite with custom mise tooling, and updated the Copier templates to use it; migrated Flask dashboards into Cockpit modules, removing ~77K lines of legacy code

On my own initiative, rebuilt the provisioning app in Rust/Tauri, backed by a server secured with Microsoft Entra ID: only approved employees and contractors can sign in to receive the device credentials it needs to automate setup, and those secrets stay in the macOS Keychain or Windows Credential Manager

Introduced AI-assisted development across the team's repositories: spec-driven development with AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex), Beads for task tracking and agent memory, and gated code review, taking the team from delegating small agent tasks to delivering whole projects with agents

Set the company's packaging and release standard: built and operate the shared CI/CD the whole company relies on, reusable GitHub Actions on a custom, spec-tested Bash framework that builds and tests Debian packages for Python, Rust, TypeScript, and generic projects on arm64 and amd64 across all three supported Ubuntu LTS releases, adopted by 30+ repositories in 3 global offices

Rebuilt the company's custom APT repository server, replacing hours-long cron-driven index rebuilds with filesystem watchers and a cached package index: packages now publish within a minute, concurrent publishes no longer corrupt the index, and build-and-test cycles dropped from hours to minutes

Built a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner platform for the company's in-house infrastructure and legacy constraints, with weekly self-updates from a scheduled workflow and a Debian caching proxy to speed up builds

As sole engineer, redesigned the device OS support packages from the ground up around Linux standards instead of home-grown conventions: product-independent Debian packages, monorepo support in the shared CI/CD, and ~44K fewer lines of legacy code; led EN 18031 security hardening across authentication, SSH access, and rate limiting

Led development of a Python service for provisioning, monitoring, and updating networked RFID and electronic article surveillance (EAS) readers; added support for three hardware families and over-the-air (OTA) firmware updates over MQTT

Automated builds of CPython 3.11–3.15 Debian packages tuned with profile-guided optimization (PGO) and link-time optimization (LTO) for three Ubuntu LTS releases, standardizing Python across product lines
Built a cross-platform device provisioning app in Python/Flet that configures devices offline over SSH

Made the standard the default: reusable Copier project templates give every new project the shared CI/CD, Debian packaging, and UI tooling from day one, including the FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, and Alembic REST service template behind Checkpoint's Readfinity Core RFID reader software
printHighlights: Replaced a 5-month, ~64K-line DDS prototype with Zenoh/MQTT in 2 weeks

work.name: Edmunds GovTech
highlights: Built an automated upgrade system that let government customers upgrade straight from several major versions behind to the latest release instead of one version at a time, saving technicians hours to days per upgrade
Designed its database migration engine for MySQL, Microsoft SQL Server, and Actian Zen (PSQL), absorbing years of schema changes previously tracked by hand in Excel
Led a team of three developers integrating Orbeon Forms into the product
Built a JavaFX application to install and manage the product's Windows services
Moved the entire codebase from System.out.println to Apache Log4j 2 with a script that analyzed each call's context
Migrated all source code from Subversion to Git and set up GitLab CI/CD
printHighlights: Built automated upgrades that took customers from several major versions behind straight to the latest, saving techs hours to days

work.name: Linode, Inc
highlights: Personally built Linode's OAuth 2.0 platform, integrating the legacy ColdFusion website and the new Python API service: single sign-on (SSO) for Linode's apps, an OAuth provider for third-party apps, and a custom SSH PAM module that authenticated access to Linode's SSH console with optional two-factor authentication (2FA)

Built reproducible local development environments, first with Vagrant and SaltStack configuration management and then Docker Compose, moving the whole stack off real servers so anyone in the company could contribute; one support engineer it opened the door for became one of the team's best developers
Championed and implemented the OpenAPI 3 specification for Linode API v4
Managed Jenkins continuous integration (CI) with GitHub Enterprise for automated testing and code quality checks
printHighlights: Built Linode's OAuth 2.0 platform: SSO for its apps, a third-party OAuth provider, and SSH console login with 2FA
Built reproducible local dev environments with Vagrant and Docker Compose, opening contributions company-wide

work.name: Mitel (formerly Ulticom, Inc)
highlights: Developed a distributed, fault-tolerant Diameter Signaling Controller on Cisco's NCS platform, integrating MongoDB for dynamic routing rules
Built its SOAP and REST APIs with Apache CXF and Jersey, hosted on an embedded Jetty server
Built a metrics collection system for observability with MySQL, Hibernate, and Protocol Buffers

work.name: Amazon.com
highlights: Developed an IP reputation system for Amazon Simple Email Service (SES) with Spring, Hibernate, and Amazon RDS
Built email deliverability monitoring that detected mail providers marking messages as junk, tracking the reputation of Amazon's mail transfer agents (MTAs)

Releases ship .deb, .rpm, and .run packages and container images from CI, with a Docusaurus docs and product site

Built a native vmnet virtio-net backend in libkrun (Rust) with packed rings, multiqueue TX, and batched syscalls

projects.name: Open-source contributions

jdx/mise and jdx/hk: OS/architecture tool filtering, and step settings inherited from groups

eclipse-paho/paho.mqtt.python, cruft, himmelblau, aube, and zensical: reconnect, packaging, and build fixes
